messages.subject: blavaan with autorun.jags
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ed,

Is there currently any way to use the autorun.jags function with blavaan so the number of sampling iterations don't have to be fixed? If not, would it be possible to export the blavaan object, run with autorun.jags, and then use the fitmeasures from blavaan on the resulting autorun object?

Thanks,
Ross

messages.subject: Re: blavaan with autorun.jags
messages.body_plain:
Use of autorun.jags is not currently possible, but it is a good idea. I will look at adding it soon.

I don't think you can currently pass an (auto)runjags object back in to blavaan, because it needs to know what model corresponds to the runjags output. But  I might be able to add this in the future...

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Need you help about "blavaan" error
messages.body_plain:
Quanying,

I can reproduce this error and will fix it soon. It is related to the two latent variables with only one observed variable (co2 and tech): the observed variable variances need to be fixed to 0, and blavaan chokes here.

Also, if this is your real dataset (as opposed to an example dataset that throws the error), I would say that your model is very complex for the data. You only have 27 observations, so the prior distributions are likely to have a strong influence on the posterior parameter values.

Finally, you should only need the "library(blavaan)" command; those other packages will be loaded automatically as needed.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: blavaan with autorun.jags
messages.body_plain:
I added a "convergence" argument to the devel version, so something like this should work:

fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy, convergence="auto")

It is worth considering this as a default option. My only worry is that autorun.jags takes a really long time for certain models, and some people might not realize why it is taking so long. Maybe I could also set the "max.time" argument to avoid really long runs, but I am open to ideas here.

Ed

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Need you help about "blavaan" error
messages.body_plain:
Quanying,

There are a few issues here:

1. There is a bug in blavaan when you have a latent variable with only one observed variable. This is not yet fixed and may take a little time (it is trickier than I initially thought).

2. I'm not sure about the goal of your analysis, so it is difficult to make suggestions. It might be helpful to talk to a local statistics expert here.

3. Keeping #2 in mind paired with the small sample size, I would remove the correlated residuals and also consider whether regression might be more suitable over SEM.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: blavaan with autorun.jags
messages.body_plain:
The devel version now has convergence="auto" as default. I had to do some guesswork about how to set default parameters here (balancing run time with desired precision of parameters), so play with it if you want and see if it seems ok.

Mauricio, the "auto" feature runs an initial sample, then looks at noise in the estimated 2.5th quantile of sampled parameters. If the noise is greater than desired, then it calculates how many more samples should be taken to reach the desired level of noise. A better summary is in the manpage of runjags::raftery.diag

Ed

> >
> > > So in setting the convergence="auto" is that then using the default psr as stopping criterion?
> >
> > Yes, it automatically uses the defaults from autorun.jags(). But you should be able to modify any of the autorun.jags arguments via blavaan's "jagcontrol" argument.
> >
> > Ed

messages.subject: Specification of priors in blavaan
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a question regarding the specification of priors in blavaan. I have a latent growth model, with an intercept and slope variable:

Model <- '

intercept =~ 1*x1+ 1*x2+ 1*x3

slope =~ 0*x1+ 1*x2+ 2*x3'

I would like to specify priors for the mean and variance of these two latent variables. To adapt the priors for the means, I understand that I have to change the alpha default prior, and for the variances I have to change the ipsi default prior.

Do I understand correctly that I can change the default prior for all parameters in alpha, but that I cannot specify a unique prior for the mean of the intercept, and a unique prior for the mean of the slope? If this is correct, do you know about another possibility to specify unique priors for the means of the intercept, and slope?

I hope someone can help me with this!

Sanne Smid
